nodes.name: Multi LLM Query
nodes.description: This node is designed to query multiple large language models (LLMs) from different providers (OpenAI, Bedrock, Gemini) using a vector database (e.g., Pinecone or FAISS) or a DataFrame. It processes user queries and returns responses by querying the selected vector database.
nodes.details:
Multi LLM Query Node Details


The Multi LLM Query node is designed to query multiple large language models (LLMs) from providers such as OpenAI, Bedrock, and Gemini, using either a vector database (e.g., Pinecone or FAISS) or a DataFrame. It processes user queries and generates responses based on the selected model and task, producing a structured DataFrame output. This node is ideal for integrating LLM-based query processing into PySpark-based data pipelines.

General:



Select Option (Task):
Specifies the task to perform. Options include:
  • summary: Generates a summary of the content in bullet points.
  • translation: Translates the content to the specified language.
  • topic_extraction: Extracts key topics from the content.
  • other: Allows for a custom task defined by the user.
Custom Prompt:
Allows users to provide a custom prompt to override the default instructions for the selected task. If left empty, the default prompt for the chosen task is used.

User Query Column:
Specifies the DataFrame column containing the user query. Default is 'userQuery'. This column provides the input query for the LLM.

Content Column:
Specifies the DataFrame column containing the text content to be processed. This is required for tasks like summary or topic extraction.

Language:
Specifies the target language for translation tasks. Default is 'en' (English). Only relevant when the task is set to 'translation'.

Model Selection:
Selects the LLM provider to use. Options are:
  • openai: Uses OpenAI models.
  • bedrock: Uses AWS Bedrock models.
  • gemini: Uses Google Gemini models.
Select Connection:
Specifies the connection details for the selected LLM provider (e.g., API keys, service configurations). This field is required to authenticate and access the chosen model.

Temperature:
Controls the randomness of the LLM's output. Default is 0 (deterministic output). Higher values (e.g., 1.0) increase creativity but may reduce consistency.

Image Column:
Specifies a DataFrame column containing base64-encoded images when processing image data. This is optional and relevant only for image or text+image modes.

Mode Selection:
Determines the input mode for the LLM. Options are:
  • text: Processes text-only input from the user query or content column.
  • image: Processes base64-encoded images from the specified image column.
  • text+image: Processes both text and base64-encoded images.

System Prompt Configuration:


System Prompt:
Allows users to define a system-level prompt to guide the LLM's behavior across all queries. This is optional and can be used to set the context or tone for the model.

Write Prompt:
Specifies the prompt text for generating the output. This can be used to fine-tune the instructions for the LLM.

Output Storage:


Output Path:
Specifies the file path where the generated output will be saved. This is optional and used when saving results to an external file.

Output Format:
Specifies the format of the saved output. Options are:
  • text: Saves the output as plain text.
  • pdf: Saves the output as a PDF file.
  • docx: Saves the output as a Microsoft Word document.

Output:


The node outputs a DataFrame with columns containing the LLM responses, typically including:
  • The original user query (from the userQueryCol).
  • The processed content (from the contentCol).
  • The generated response from the LLM.
  • Additional metadata (e.g., model used, task performed) depending on the configuration.
nodes.examples:
Example: Multi LLM Query Node



Input:


A DataFrame contains the following data:
- userQuery: ["Summarize this article", "Translate this to Spanish", "Extract key topics"]
- content: ["A detailed article about climate change impacts...", "A report on renewable energy sources...", "A study on AI advancements..."]
- imageData: [null, null, "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUg..."]

The Multi LLM Query node is configured as follows:
  • Select Option (Task): ["summary", "translation", "topic_extraction"]
  • Custom Prompt: Empty (uses default prompts for each task)
  • User Query Column: userQuery
  • Content Column: content
  • Language: es (Spanish, for translation task)
  • Model Selection: openai
  • Select Connection: Configured with valid OpenAI API key
  • Temperature: 0.7
  • Image Column: imageData
  • Mode Selection: text+image
  • System Prompt: "You are a helpful assistant providing accurate and concise responses."
  • Write Prompt: "Generate clear and concise output based on the user query."
  • Output Path: /data/output/llm_results/
  • Output Format: text

Output:


The node processes the DataFrame and produces a DataFrame with the following structure:

userQuery | response
--------------------------|----------------------------------------------
Summarize this article | - Impacts on ecosystems - Rising sea levels...
Translate this to Spanish | Un informe sobre fuentes de energía renovable...
Extract key topics | - Machine learning - Neural networks...

Explanation:


- The first row processes the "summary" task, generating a bullet-point summary of the climate change article using the OpenAI model. No image data is used (imageData is null).
- The second row processes the "translation" task, translating the renewable energy report into Spanish (language set to 'es'). No image data is used.
- The third row processes the "topic_extraction" task, extracting key topics from the AI advancements study. The imageData column is present but ignored since the task is text-based.
- The System Prompt ensures the LLM provides concise and accurate responses.
- The output is saved as plain text files in /data/output/llm_results/ due to the Output Format setting.
- The temperature of 0.7 allows for some variability in the responses while maintaining coherence.
- Since Mode Selection is set to text+image, the node is capable of processing images if provided, but in this case, only the third row has image data, which is not used for the topic_extraction task.
